intro: Newest first. The engine was rebuilt so every plume is a two-faced 3D ribbon of cloth; colour comes only from which face is toward the viewer. Single plumes are recreated from references and reviewed by independent critics who have not seen the code; then five original plumes are reviewed against the references.

rounds.title: Stages 1–2 · volute, stem, fold
rounds.note: Stage 1: a single volute with tangent entry, curvature rising steadily as it winds in (checked numerically), and an open eye. Stage 2: one stem with one recursive cluster (lobes splitting into unequal, forward-hooking leaflets), 78% of the stem left bare, and a turnover: the strip narrows, an oblique crease crosses it, the red lip rolls over in front and the lining shows beyond.

rounds.title: Round 1 · reviewed
critique: Garter: the red bands are bare, even-width tubes ending in tight snail spirals, like tentacles; in the reference every band is a flat acanthus leaf with lobes along its length and open leafy curls.
Garter: the white fans are thin upright stalks with crumpled tops; the reference has broad, layered fans spreading sideways at mid-height.
Stirling: a flat, wide starburst of long horizontal blades instead of a compact upright mass of stacked heavy lobes.
Stirling: no gathered grey cloth behind the helm; the top curls are smooth ram's-horn spirals.
Both: leaf tips are crumpled frills; no band twists to show its lining; shading is a stepped gradient that ignores the turns.
fixes: Garter bands narrowed and made leafy on both edges over shared intervals (the 40% bare rule counts overlaps once); fans broadened and turned sideways.
Stirling recomposed as a compact upright mass over a gathered grey body.
Engine: leaflets too small to read as fingers are dropped (no frills); strips shaded flatter; the inside of each turn and the underside of each curl now darken (curvature-aware shading).

rounds.title: Round 2 · reviewed
critique: Garter: the white lining fans are almost missing; the whole mantling reads as solid red.
Garter: the red bands are thin round hoses laid over a separate clump of leaves, not wide flat lobed ribbons.
Stirling: no gathered grey cloth at the helm; the grey stands up as tall smooth fans and big snail volutes.
Stirling: long red horns stick out sideways, giving a spiky diamond outline; lower tubes end in small tufts.
Both: leaf tips are single pointed blades; shading shows stepped bands.
fixes: Garter: eight broad, many-ribbed white fans reaching past the red; the separate leaf clump removed and its lobes grown from the bands; bands widened with swells.
Stirling: nine short, broad grey folds gathered at the helm's base and shoulders, paler curls kept small; the sideways horns pulled upright.
Engine: volute inner-rim returns made narrower and stopped short of the eye; finer shading levels (72).

rounds.title: Round 3 · reviewed
critique: Garter: the scroll eyes are thick pale rings with a red clump inside; the red band itself should roll into an open red volute with leaves on its rim, the lining only a sliver.

Garter: the bands run flat and cross in a stiff X; in the reference they climb in S-curves to tall volutes at the top corners and drop to lower volutes beside the shield, framing the silhouette in a wide M.
Garter: the white fans are long bare blades radiating in a V; they should be short, dense and serrated along their length, layered close beside the helm.
Stirling: red strands converge on the helm crown in a sunburst; the gathered grey mass should sit beside the helm with upright lobes rising from it.
Stirling: the lower arcs are smooth tentacles without leafy scroll endings; leaf tips on both are frilled tongues; stepped shading bands.
fixes: Garter: the folds before the volutes removed so the red band rolls into open red eyes, with lobes on the coil's outer rim.
Garter: the upper band rebuilt to climb in an S to a tall corner volute and the lower band to drop beside the shield into a second volute, both throwing lobes off the outer edge.
Garter: nine shorter, denser fans layered close to the helm with serrations at mid-length and tip.

rounds.title: Round 4 · after three rounds of fixes (final review: remaining defects)
rounds.note: Not fixed yet. These are the open defects found by a fourth, independent review.
critique: Stirling: the red is a spray of long thin straps radiating from the helm with ruffled tufts; it should be a few short, heavy, deeply cut lobe-stacks standing upright on each side.

Stirling: the gathered grey cloth is still mostly hidden, and a V-shaped gap above the helm splits the outline into two wings; it needs a central grey drapery mass and a red band bridging the top into a squared block.

Garter: the upper stems cross in an X above the helm and all four end in thin fiddlehead coils; the bands should leave the helm sideways, widen and taper like cloth, show lining at turnovers, and roll into large open eyes with lobes along the curl.
Garter: the white reads as a cauliflower clump between the X arms; it should be two wing-like fans at helm height of long pointed fronds radiating outward in layers.
Both: every leaf is the same flame-shaped ruffled tuft rather than a lobe divided into 3–5 serrated, forward-hooking fingers spread along the stem; shading still bands along the length.

rounds.title: Two-faced engine · single-plume recreations
rounds.note: Scores from independent critics (grace / shape, out of 10). Blue lion: r1 3/3, r2 3/2, r3 2/2. Saint Larry: r1 3/3. The latest renders (blue lion r4, Saint Larry r2) have not been scored.

images.caption: Saint Larry, right middle plume · latest

critique: Too much bare band and too little foliage: the stem should be swallowed by a few broad leaves.
Lobes read as spikes, slivers or fins stuck on the band rather than broad acanthus leaves grown from its edge, with rounded fingers and deep rounded notches.
Lining is scattered as many small chips; the references show it in a few continuous places: along a rolled edge, inside a scroll, at a twisted tip.
Gesture and silhouette differ (crossing straps, vertical spikes) where the references flow in one continuous S.
Curls end as open hooks; the references close into tight volutes with a small knob of lining.

rounds.title: Two-faced engine · five original plumes

images.caption: Wave crest, Double scroll, Flame fronds, Upright fronds, Falling turn-overs
The references they were judged against

rounds.note: Critic scores: Wave crest 4, Double scroll 3, Flame fronds 2, Upright fronds 3, Falling turn-overs 4 (out of 10). Closest in spirit: Wave crest.
critique: Lobes are sawtooth or stair-stepped rather than rounded, swelling, teardrop fingers with deep rounded notches.
Each plume is a single thin strand; the references branch quickly into several decreasing branches, each ending in a scroll or leaf cluster.
Turn-overs read as colour switches at a seam rather than a visible roll with a curved fold edge.
Terminals end in claws and spikes instead of spiral volutes.
Surface shading looks faceted and crumpled rather than smooth painted colour with a midrib following each lobe.
